name.text: C8.Q1 — The Grover iterate and the optimal number of steps

questiontext.text:
C8.Q1 — Two reflections make a rotation

\(G=D\,O_f\) rotates the state by \(2\theta\) in the good/bad plane, with \(\sin\theta=\sqrt{M/N}\).

Write grover_operator(N, marked) returning the explicit \(N\times N\) iterate; optimal_iterations(N, M) returning \(\lfloor\pi/(4\arcsin\sqrt{M/N})\rfloor\) as an int; and success_probability(N, M, k) returning \(\sin^{2}((2k+1)\theta)\) rounded to 6 decimals.

optimal_iterations(1024, 1) -> 25
success_probability(16, 1, 3) -> 0.961319

testcode.text: import numpy as np G = grover_operator(8, [3]) print(np.allclose(G.conj().T @ G, np.eye(8)))

name.text: C8.Q2 — Running Grover, and overcooking it

questiontext.text:
C8.Q2 — The periodicity of the success probability

Because \(G\) is a rotation, iterating past \(k_{\text{opt}}\) decreases the success probability — a purely quantum failure mode with no classical analogue.

Write run_grover(N, marked, k) returning the state after \(k\) iterations starting from the uniform superposition, and marked_probability(psi, marked) returning the total probability on the marked indices, rounded to 6 decimals. Then best_k(N, marked, kmax) returning the \(k\le k_{\max}\) maximising that probability.

N=16, one marked: probabilities peak at k=3 and fall again by k=6

name.text: C8.Q3 — Amplitude amplification with an arbitrary state preparation

questiontext.text:
C8.Q3 — Beyond the uniform superposition

Replace \(H^{\otimes n}\) by any \(A\) with \(A|0\rangle=|\psi\rangle\). Then \(Q=-A S_0 A^{\dagger} S_f\) amplifies the good component at the same quadratic rate, with \(\sin\theta=\|\Pi_{\text{good}}|\psi\rangle\|\).

Write amplitude_amplification_operator(A, marked) returning \(Q=-A S_0 A^{\dagger} S_f\) (with \(S_0=I-2|0\rangle\langle0|\) and \(S_f\) the phase oracle), and amplify(A, marked, k) returning the state after \(k\) applications of \(Q\) to \(A|0\rangle\).

With A = H^{tensor n} this reproduces the Grover iterate up to sign.

question.answer:
import numpy as np
def amplitude_amplification_operator(A, marked): A = np.asarray(A, dtype=complex) N = A.shape[0] S0 = np.eye(N, dtype=complex) S0[0, 0] = -1 Sf = np.eye(N, dtype=complex) for m in marked: Sf[m, m] = -1 return -A @ S0 @ A.conj().T @ Sf
def amplify(A, marked, k): A = np.asarray(A, dtype=complex) N = A.shape[0] e0 = np.zeros(N, dtype=complex) e0[0] = 1 psi = A @ e0 Q = amplitude_amplification_operator(A, marked) for _ in range(k): psi = Q @ psi return psi

testcode.text: import numpy as np H = np.array([[1,1],[1,-1]], dtype=complex)/np.sqrt(2) A = np.array([[1.0+0j]]) for _ in range(4): A = np.kron(A, H) print(round(float(abs(amplify(A, [5], 0)[5])**2), 6))
import numpy as np H = np.array([[1,1],[1,-1]], dtype=complex)/np.sqrt(2) A = np.array([[1.0+0j]]) for _ in range(4): A = np.kron(A, H) psi = amplify(A, [5], 3) print(round(float(abs(psi[5])**2), 6))

import numpy as np H = np.array([[1,1],[1,-1]], dtype=complex)/np.sqrt(2) A = np.array([[1.0+0j]]) for _ in range(3): A = np.kron(A, H) Q = amplitude_amplification_operator(A, [2]) print(np.allclose(Q.conj().T @ Q, np.eye(8)))

import numpy as np rng = np.random.default_rng(6) M = rng.normal(size=(8,8)) + 1j*rng.normal(size=(8,8)) A, _ = np.linalg.qr(M) psi0 = amplify(A, [3], 0) psi1 = amplify(A, [3], 1) print(abs(psi1[3])**2 > abs(psi0[3])**2)
import numpy as np H = np.array([[1,1],[1,-1]], dtype=complex)/np.sqrt(2) A = np.array([[1.0+0j]]) for _ in range(2): A = np.kron(A, H) print(round(float(abs(amplify(A, [1], 1)[1])**2), 6))

name.text: C8.Q4 — Quantum counting by amplitude estimation

questiontext.text:
C8.Q4 — Estimating M without finding a marked item

The Grover iterate has eigenvalues \(e^{\pm2i\theta}\) on the good/bad plane. Phase estimation on \(G\) therefore returns \(\theta\), and \(M=N\sin^{2}\theta\).

Write grover_angle(N, M) returning \(\theta=\arcsin\sqrt{M/N}\); counting_estimate(N, y, t) returning the estimate \(N\sin^{2}(\pi y/2^{t})\) rounded to 4 decimals; and counting_error_bound(N, M, t) returning the worst-case bound \(2\pi\sqrt{M(N-M)}/2^{t}+\pi^{2}N/4^{t}\), rounded to 4 decimals.

N=256, M=4  ->  theta ~ 0.1253
counting_estimate(256, 5, 6) -> 15.1141
